also: pay attention to what I say

terms.gloss: mark my words, pay attention to what I say
terms.comment: Built on animum intendere in + acc., to turn one’s mind to (Cic. Ac. 2.46, Sall. Jug. 20.1, Lewis & Short); to more than one, intendite. Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

terms.gloss: mind my words, listen to me
terms.comment: auscultāre, to listen to, is chiefly a word of comedy (Lewis & Short: frequent before the classical period, rare in it). Every word is classical; we have found no classical instance of the phrase.

sources: Lewis & Short: intendo · Lewis & Short: ausculto
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency (printed page numbers): p. 343.
